title: First Mile — Operational FunnelSheet
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, runnable sheet for the "first mile" of a rollout: a single-page operational funnel that ties sprint milestones to top-line KPIs, owner-level readiness checks, and immediate fallback actions. Designed as a working doc for on-call and launch ops during the first 14 days after a constrained beta or small- cohort public release.

Context and scope:
- Focus: early-stage user flow that exercise hosted API + Dedicated routing paths.
- Goal: move from canary (0.1% traffic) -> phase-1 (1% traffic) -> ramp (10%) across 3 sprints while keeping latency and cost guardrails intact.
- Audience: product-ops lead, release engineer, SRE duty, ME/solutions on-call, and product PM.

How to use this sheet (quick):
1) At start of each day, update the KPI snapshot row (actuals).
2) For any KPI in amber/red, trigger the corresponding contingency listed in the right column.
3) Owners update their readiness ticks in the morning standup and mark blockers (TODO: link to blocker board).

Sprint timeline (high level):
- Sprint A (days 0–3): Canary smoke + mission control staffing.
  - Primary focus: functional correctness, basic SLOs, and feature telemetry.
- Sprint B (days 4–7): Phase-1 ramp to 1% traffic.
  - Primary focus: capacity signals, latency percentiles, error budgets.
- Sprint C (days 8–14): Ramp to 10% traffic for cohort/surge test.
  - Primary focus: cost burn analysis, model fallback performance, and user-impact metrics.

Top-line KPI tracker (single-row snapshot per day; update numbers each AM):
- Daily active requests (hosted + dedicated): baseline 10k/day expected at 10% ramp.
- 95th latency (ms): target < 350ms; amber > 350ms; red > 600ms.
- Error rate (5xx + client retries): target < 0.5%; amber 0.5–2%; red > 2%.
- Cost per 1k tokens (USD): expected range $0.85–$1.40; amber > $1.6; red > $2.0.
- Quality regression (prompt set F1 delta): target delta ≤ 2%; amber 2–5%; red > 5%.

Operational funnel (columns you should fill each day):
- Date | Traffic cohort % | Actual requests | 95th latency | Error rate | Cost/1k tokens | Quality delta | Owner | Readiness tick | Contingency invoked? | Notes
- (example) 2025-02-01 | 0.1% | 120 | 210ms | 0.12% | $0.92 | 0.6% | Liam O'Connor | infra:green, model:amber | fallback-model-2 | warm cache triggered

Owner roster and primary responsibilities (quick mapping):
- Product-ops lead: Asha Patel — overall go/no-go, cross-team escalation.
- Release engineer: Liam O'Connor — rollout orchestration, feature flags.
- SRE duty: Noah Chen — infra scaling, latency SLOs, autoscale tuning.
- Solutions/ME on-call: Priya Rao — customer-impact triage, canary customer outreach.
- Applied ML contact: Mariana Gomez — model quality regressions, rollback decisions.

Readiness checklist (per owner, tick at start of each sprint):
- Infra (SRE)
  - Autoscaling policies verified for 2x expected peak.
  - Redis/KV cache warming plan created and tested.
  - Circuit-breakers and throttles in place with documented thresholds.
- Model (Applied ML)
  - Canary model validated on synthetic prompt set (baseline suite).
  - Secondary fallback model packaged and smoke-tested.
  - Perf/quantization profile recorded for each model variant.
- Release (Release Eng)
  - Feature-flag gating configured with kill-switch.
  - Rollout runbook published and distributed to on-call.
  - Health-check endpoints documented and instrumented in console.
- Product & Support
  - Beta customer list pre-notified and support playbook ready.
  - Messaging templates prepared for escalation scenarios.

Contingency and immediate actions (mapped to KPI states):
- Latency amber (95p 350–600ms):
  - Action: enable reduced batching (lower throughput but reduces queuing), pre-warm smaller pools; notify infra owner; engage de-opt routing to cheaper/regional pool if available.
  - Escalation window: 30–60 minutes.
- Latency red (>600ms):
  - Action: initiate traffic rollback by 50% for affected cohort; activate model-fallback to fast-variant; open incident channel; pause ramp.
  - Escalation: page SRE lead and product-ops.
- Error rate amber (0.5–2%):
  - Action: check recent deploys/PRs, verify model input validation errors, increase retries with exponential backoff.
- Error rate red (>2%):
  - Action: immediate rollback of recent release, reduce traffic to zero for offending path, escalate to on-call triage.
- Quality regression amber/red:
  - Action: stop rollout to new customers, run A/B diff on failing prompt set, consider quick revert to previous model.

Capacity simulation notes (quick knobs):
- For expected surge of 10x baseline, ensure buffer of 1.5x GPU pools and cold-start budget of 20% for burst.
- Batching policy: prefer dynamic batching with 60ms wait cap for user-facing flows, reduce to 10ms for latency-sensitive tests.
- KV cache hit target: >= 60% for prefix-heavy workloads; if hit < 45%, schedule cache rekey + warm window.

Decision gates (go/no-go heuristics to proceed to next cohort):
- Gate A -> B (0.1% -> 1%): all green or only isolated amber in non-critical KPIs; error rate <0.5%; 95th <450ms; costs within 1.5x of estimate.
- Gate B -> C (1% -> 10%): latency under 350ms 95th for last 4 hours; cost burn projection within budget window; fallback model verified.

Open questions / risks (notes to self):
- Do we have automatic cross-region fallback configured for Dedicated customers? (PENDING: infra ticket).
- Are billing alerts tuned for short-lived cost spikes from retries?
- How to capture user-level quality loss signals (beyond eval prompt set) in first-24h? log/flagging approach?

Action items (immediate):
- [ ] Release eng: add kill-switch to rollout pipeline (Liam).
- [ ] SRE: run autoscale soak test during quiet hours (Noah).
- [ ] Applied ML: finalize fallback perf profile and document observed delta (Mariana).
- [ ] Product-ops: prep one-pager for exec (Asha).

Quick links and artifacts:
- Blocker board (jira): JIRA:PRODOPS-4212
- Canary telemetry dashboard: console/telemetry/canary-firstmile (internal)
- Runbook draft: confluence:PRODOPS-FirstMile-Runbook-Draft

Notes/voice: this doc is intentionally terse — it’s a live, mutable checklist for the first two weeks. Use the daily snapshot to drive standup actions and keep the contingencies column updated. If a checklist item is unresolved at the end of the sprint, tag as escalation and move into the release retrospective.
